title: Lane Discipline & One-Way Streets
whatItIs: Keep to the left unless you are overtaking or turning right, and pick your lane early. In one-way streets traffic can pass on both sides.
keyFacts: Keep to the left-hand lane unless road signs or markings tell you otherwise.
On a two-lane dual carriageway, use the right-hand lane only to overtake or turn right, then move back.
On a three-lane single carriageway, use the middle lane only to overtake or turn right: oncoming traffic can too.
Follow lane arrows and get into the right lane in good time. Don't change lanes suddenly.

keyFacts.text: In a one-way street, traffic MUST go in the direction shown by the signs.

items.title: Turning left
items.text: Use the left-hand lane, unless signs or markings say otherwise.

items.title: Turning right
items.text: Use the right-hand lane, unless signs or markings say otherwise.

items.title: Going straight ahead
items.text: Use the most suitable lane for where you are going.

items.title: Traffic on both sides
items.text: Others may pass you on the left or the right. Check both mirrors.

a.label: Dual carriageway, 2 lanes
points: Right lane: overtaking or turning right
Move back left when it is safe

b.label: Single carriageway, 3 lanes
points: Middle lane shared with oncoming traffic
Overtake only if it is clear

onTheTest.question: You are in a one-way street and want to turn right. Which lane should you use?
onTheTest.why: Unless signs or markings say otherwise, use the right-hand lane to turn right in a one-way street.

traps: In a one-way street you can be passed on either side.
Don't sit in the right lane of a dual carriageway once you have overtaken.
On a three-lane road, oncoming drivers may use the middle lane too.

sources.ref: Rules 133 to 143 (Multi-lane carriageways and one-way streets)
